To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) people adapt to the perceived sincerity of others; (2) people perceive sincerity in written text; (3) the perceived sincerity in written text is influenced by psycholinguistic properties; (4) people's perception of sincerity is influenced by their own sincerity.
the perception of sincerity can be decoded from written language, and that this perception is related to the perceived personality of the writer.

the following psycholinguistic factors are associated with perceived sincerity: (i) the use of the first person singular pronoun I, (ii) the use of a large proportion of first person pronouns, (iii) the use of first person singular pronouns in combination with the past tense, (iv) the use of past tense in general, (v) the use of present tense, (vi) the use of future tense, (vii) the use and proportion of positive words
